title: Introduce credential-profile-matrix and ergonomic stream adapters across Python/TypeScript/Go
author: Aisha Kumaran
release_notes: Backwards-compatible credential preset matrix and ergonomic stream adapters for Py/TS/Go. Version bumps: python-sdk v1.28.0, ts-sdk v2.3.1, go-sdk v1.5.0. Includes telemetry tags for retry profiles and stream progress hooks.
description:
Context: Multiple teams have implemented ad-hoc credential retry and session warmup logic across SDKs, leading to subtle mismatches in behavior (token fall-through, heartbeat timing, and retry categorization). This PR consolidates a small, opinionated credential-profile matrix, exposes ergonomic stream adapters (progress hooks and peekable cursors), and aligns retry telemetry across Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs.

What this change does: Unified credential-profile-matrix: a small table of named profiles (default, high-throughput, low-latency, delegated-refresh) that map to TTLs, prefetch heuristics, and retry presets. SDKs accept a profile name and translate it to local config. Ergonomic stream adapters: lightweight pullstream/pushstream facades with optional progress hooks (emit progress events at prefix/kv cache warmup boundaries), peekable cursor support for graceful backpressure, and a small adapter layer to normalize async iterators across languages. Retry telemetry: add named telemetry tags (cred_profile, retry_preset, stream_hint) emitted with user-facing request spans so ops can correlate cost with credential behavior. Cross-SDK parity: implementation in Python, TypeScript, and Go with identical surface-level semantics and automated interop tests. Version bumps: python-sdk -> v1.28.0, ts-sdk -> v2.3.1, go-sdk -> v1.5.0.

Migration notes: This is backwards-compatible by default: existing callers continue to work with implicit "default" profile. Customers that explicitly set per-field retry/ttl in their config will be mapped to the closest profile with a deprecation warning (automated shim). Teams who want to adopt the new profiles can pass profile names in client constructors or use env var REDWOOD_CRED_PROFILE.

Testing and rollout: Unit tests added to each SDK, crosslang interop test that spins up a lightweight mock auth service and verifies token handoff/refresh semantics under contention. E2E scripts exercise stream adapters under synthetic load to verify progress hooks and backpressure. CI: flaky test in go SDK (lease_timer_test) required a timing tolerance adjustment and an explicit retry in the CI job; flake ticket created: ENG-3053. Rollout plan: staged release (canary -> stable) coordinated with client library publishers; monitor cred-related error rates and retry counts in the Redwood Console.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement credential-profile-matrix in Py/TS/Go
- [x] Add ergonomic stream adapters with progress hooks and peek cursors
- [x] Emit standardized retry/cred telemetry tags
- [x] Add unit and integration tests, interop harness
- [x] Bump SDK versions and update changelogs
- [x] Docs: add section in SDK auth guide and streaming ergonomics

Notes for reviewers: The diff touches auth plumbing in three SDKs and introduces a small common spec (credential-profile mapping) in the repo under /docs/sdk/cred-profiles.md. The adapters are intentionally minimal: surface-level sugar only, no changes to wire protocols. If you want stricter behavior, we can follow up with an opt-in strict mode.

Related: ENG-2941, SUP-481, ENG-3053
